run: Rare 1976, Versailles 1985, the Van Cleef and Arpels edition and the tiara
the marriage of 1838 and the name Piper-Heidsieck
Rémy Martin's purchase of 1988 and the sale to EPI of 2011
a label of the house for its letters
Rare as a house of its own in 2018 and Rare Rosé's first vintage
searches.note: Thirty searches of a share of thirty two for chunk h5, none of them the author's; two left unspent. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the people and their dates, the village, the kind of producer, every change of hands, the grapes, the sites, the first vintage, the rhythm, the lees, the dosage, the bottle, the other cuvées, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries; the lint was run after every change.

tested.founded: 1785 and the Westphalian cloth merchant: the library, Wikipedia and merchants; the Marie Antoinette meeting as legend. Confirmed.
tested.kind: NM 211 001 on a Cuvée Brut label in the Open Food Facts database; the DGCCRF defines NM.
tested.story: The marriage of 1838: Wikipedia and merchants, the label name 1845 by one merchant (reworded). Rémy Martin's purchase of 1988: the Rémy Cointreau reference document. EPI: signed 31 May and completed 8 July 2011, by the market filings and Rémy Cointreau's release. Rare its own house in September or October 2018: two trade accounts. Hors-Série 1971 announced 7 September 2021, disgorged February 2021, held back from the Cuvée Florens Louis 1971: the house and Falstaff.
tested.cuvee: First vintage 1976, unveiled at Versailles in 1985: several accounts. Rare 2013: 70 per cent Chardonnay, 30 Pinot Noir, 11 crus, eight years on lees and a year under cork, disgorged December 2022, 9 grams a litre: Decanter, K and L and the importer's sheet. Rare Rosé first vintage 2007: Decanter and the drinks business. Vintage list: trade accounts add 1985 and 2015.
tested.also: Hors-Série 1971 in equal parts Pinot Noir and Chardonnay: Forbes Brasil and the author's Decanter; the house's first limited edition by its own release.
tested.table: Read aloud: house45's label year reworded; cuvee45's count removed; the rest carries only sourced claims.
tested.cards: Three cards and three questions read: one right answer each (Rare; 1785; Chardonnay), plausible wrong ones (Cristal, Hemera, Celebris; 1729, 1772, 1851; Pinot Noir, Meunier, Pinot Blanc), no length clue.

changes.was: the two names were joined on the label (in 1838)
changes.now: the two names came together as Piper-Heidsieck, after the marriage of 1838
changes.why: Wikipedia and several merchants date the marriage to 1838, but one merchant's history dates the name Piper-Heidsieck on the label to 1845, so the year of the label is not told.

changes.was: In 2018 Rare was given a name and a house of its own
changes.now: In 2018 Rare became a house of its own
changes.why: Rare bore its name from 1976; what came in 2018 (September or October by account) was the house of its own.
sources: the drinks business: Rare Champagne as a brand of its own, 2018

changes.was: ... by the house; the gold work on the everyday bottle carries that memory.
changes.now: ... by the house and a trade account.
changes.why: No source carries the clause; the tiara on the standard bottle is credited to Arthus-Bertrand by some accounts and Fabergé by others, never to the 1985 edition, so the clause was the author's reading and is cut, as the author asked.
sources: Wine Paris: Rare Champagne exhibitor page

changes.was: Its own pages list eleven: 1976 ... 2013; eleven of them on its pages between 1976 and 2013
changes.now: its own pages have listed eleven, from 1976 to 2013, and trade accounts add a 1985 and a 2015; the spoken line says only that it is made in declared years
changes.why: Two trade accounts name a 1985 and a 2015 (the 2015 unveiled at Versailles), so the count of eleven is what the house's pages showed, not the whole list; the table line no longer gives a count that will not hold.
sources: Wine Paris: Rare Champagne exhibitor page

open: The 1985 and 2015 vintages rest on trade accounts, not on the house's own list as the author read it.
The founder's dates (1749 to 1828) stand on Wikipedia alone, so he stays described.
Hors-Série 1971's 2,021 bottles now have two trade accounts (Wine Industry Advisor, a Luxembourg trade page) but are still left out as a figure that serves no question.
Vessels and malolactic were not found by this refuter either.
codexInTension: WINE_PRODUCERS p-piper-heidsieck: its why names the founder Florens-Louis Heidsieck without dates, his dates resting on one source; the record describes him instead.
